CHIEF COMPLAINT
Knee pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
62-year-old male with past medical history of kidney transplant, hypothyroidism, and arthritis who presents with complaints of bilateral knee pain. Patient reports pain began over the weekend while moving boxes up and down basement stairs. By end of day, both knees were painful, with pain being equal bilaterally. Patient has had some knee problems in the past but attributes current pain to repetition and weight of boxes. Patient attempted treatment with Tylenol and ice but reports nothing really seemed to help. Pain kept patient up Saturday night. Denies fever, chills, muscle aches, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies fever, chills, muscle aches, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or headaches. No other symptoms reported.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Kidney transplant (for polycystic kidneys, performed a few years ago), hypothyroidism, arthritis

MEDICATIONS
Immunosuppressive medications, Synthroid

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: No fever. Heart rate and blood pressure normal. Cardiac exam: 2/6 systolic ejection murmur appreciated, stable. Knee exam: Right knee with edema and erythema, pain to palpation, and decreased range of motion. Left knee appears fine.

RESULTS
Right knee x-ray: Good bony alignment, no acute fracture. Labs: White blood cell count not elevated. Kidney function very good.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Knee pain/acute exacerbation of arthritis: Prescribed Ultram 50 mg every 6 hours as needed. Patient advised to take it easy. Autoimmune panel ordered. If symptoms continue, further imaging and possible referral to physical therapy will be considered.
2. Hypothyroidism: Continue Synthroid. Thyroid panel ordered.
3. Arthritis: Continue current management. Patient counseled that certain anti-inflammatory medications cannot be used due to kidney transplant. Will monitor over next couple weeks and refer to physical therapy if needed.
